edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: pregnant women, infants, or young children
edges.mechanism: The proposed route is immune programming: maternal or infant probiotic exposure may shift early Th1/Th2 balance and barrier maturation in ways that reduce atopic dermatitis risk.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2025 Wang meta analysis in Front Pediatr already points to multi-strain probiotics in pregnancy or infancy tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
